L20@P0: Treatment of advanced (unresectable or metastatic) melanoma in adults C43 00431a ODMS:
L21@P0: Ipilimumab:
L22@P0: 09/10/2017
L23@P0: Nivolumab (IV):
L24@P0: 09/10/2017
L25@P0: Nivolumab (SC):
L26@P0: 01/01/2026
L27@P0: First-line treatment of adult patients with unresectable or advanced
L28@P0: hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)
L29@P0: C22 00431b N/A
L30@P0: * This applies to post 2012 indications
L31@P0: Please note that this regimen reflects the updated dosing posology for nivolumab from May 2018.
L32@P0: TREATMENT:
L33@P0: The starting dose of the drugs detailed below may be adjusted downward by the prescribing clinician, using their independent medical
L34@P0: judgement, to consider each patient’s individual clinical circumstances.
L35@P0: Cycles 1-4:
L36@P0: Nivolumab and ipilimumab are administered on Day 1 of a 21-day cycle for the first 4 cycles.
L37@P0: From cycle 5 onwards:
L38@P0: Nivolumab is administered as monotherapy at a dose of 240mg IV or 600mg SC on Day 1 of a 14-Day cycle
L39@P0: (Ref NCCP Regimen 00483) or 480mg IV or 1200mg SC on Day 1 of a 28-Day cycle (Ref NCCP Regimen 00484).
L40@P0: For the monotherapy phase, the first dose of nivolumab should be administered as follows:
L41@P0: For melanoma:
L42@P0: • 3 weeks after the last dose of the combination of nivolumab and ipilimumab if using the 240mg IV
L43@P0: or 600mg SC every 14 days schedule
L44@P0: or
L45@P0: • 6 weeks after the last dose of the combination of nivolumab and ipilimumab if using the 480mg IV
L46@P0: or 1200mg SC every 28 days schedule
L47@P0: For HCC:
L48@P0: • 3 weeks after the last dose of the combination of nivolumab and ipilimumab
L49@P0: Monotherapy phase duration for melanoma:
L50@P0: Nivolumab should continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.
L51@P0: Monotherapy phase duration for HCC:
L52@P0: Nivolumab should continue for up to 24 months unless patient experiences disease progression or
L53@P0-1: unacceptable toxicity.NCCP National SACT Regimen

L66@P1: Switching monotherapy (i.e. cycle 5 onwards) dosing schedule:
L67@P1: Switching from a 2-weekly to a 4-weekly schedule:
L68@P1: • the first 4-weekly dose (480mg for IV or 1200mg for SC) should be administered two weeks after the
L69@P1: last 2-weekly dose (240mg for IV or 600mg for SC)
L70@P1: Switching from 4-weekly to 2-weekly schedule:
L71@P1: • the first 2-weekly dose (240mg for IV or 600mg for SC) dose should be administered four weeks after
L72@P1: the last 4-weekly dose (480mg for IV or 1200mg for SC)
L73@P1: Patients should be monitored continuously (at least up to 5 months after the last dose) as an adverse reaction
L74@P1: with nivolumab in combination with ipilimumab may occur at any time during or after discontinuation of
L75@P1: therapy.
L76@P1: Facilities to treat anaphylaxis MUST be present when systemic anti-cancer therapy (SACT) is administered.

L125@P2: ALTERNATIVE TREATMENT SCHEDULE:
L126@P2: Table 3: Treatment Schedule for Nivolumab (SC) Monotherapy (cycle 5 onwards)
L127@P2: Drug Dose Route Diluent & Rate Cycle
L128@P2: Nivolumab 600mgaSCc* Over 3-5 minutes Every 14 days
L129@P2:  OR
L130@P2: Nivolumab 1200mgbSCc* Over 3-5 minutes Every 28 days
L131@P2: aAllow one 600mg vial to reach room temperature, then withdraw 5 mL of solution for injection into the syringe.
L132@P2: bAllow two 600mg vials to reach room temperature, then withdraw 10 mL of solution for injection into the syringe.
L133@P2: c May be administered subcutaneously using a 23G-25G hypodermic injection needle or subcutaneous administration set (e.g., winged/butterfly)
L134@P2: The hypodermic injection needle must be attached to the syringe immediately prior to administration to avoid clogging.
L135@P2: The dose should not be split between two syringes or between two sites of administration.
L136@P2: Inject into the subcutaneous tissue of the left or right thigh or abdomen. Alternate injection sites for successive injections.
L137@P2: Do not inject at other sites of the body.
L138@P2: Do not inject into areas where the skin is tender, red, or bruised, or areas where there are scars or moles.
L139@P2: If the administration of nivolumab SC injection is interrupted, it can be resumed at the same site, or at an alternate site.
L140@P2: During the treatment course with nivolumab SC, other medicinal products for subcutaneous administration should preferably be injected at different
L141@P2: sites.
L142@P2: *See alternative treatment schedule for nivolumab IV above.
L143@P2: ELIGIBILITY:
L144@P2: All indications:
L145@P2: • Indications as above
L146@P2: • ECOG status 0-2
L147@P2: • Adequate haematological, hepatic and renal function
L148@P2: • Nivolumab and ipilimumab are not recommended during pregnancy and in women of childbearing
L149@P2: potential not using effective contraception unless prescribing consultant deems clinical benefit
L150@P2: outweighs the potential risk. Effective contraception should be used for at least 5 months following
L151@P2: the last dose of nivolumab
L152@P2: 
L153@P2: In patients with HCC:
L154@P2: • Child-Pugh Score: 5 or 6
L155@P2: CAUTIONS:
L156@P2: • Patients with clinically significant autoimmune disease
L157@P2: • Immunosuppressive doses of systemic corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive medication(s)
L158@P2: (defined as > 10mg prednisoLONE/day (or steroid equivalent), excluding inhaled or topical steroids)
L159@P2: • Any active clinically significant infection requiring therapy
L160@P2: • Symptomatic CNS metastases
L161@P2: • Symptomatic interstitial lung disease
L162@P2: EXCLUSIONS:
L163@P2: • Hypersensitivity to ipilimumab, nivolumab or any of the excipients
L164@P2: • Information regarding prior therapy with an anti PD-1 or anti PD-L1 antibody Available on the NCCP
L165@P2-3: website NCCP National SACT Regimen

L178@P3: PRESCRIPTIVE AUTHORITY:
L179@P3: The treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist.
L180@P3: TESTS:
L181@P3: Baseline tests:
L182@P3: • FBC, renal and liver profile
L183@P3: • Blood glucose
L184@P3: • Thyroid function tests (TFTs)
L185@P3: Disease-specific baseline test:
L186@P3: • Advanced melanoma: determination of BRAF status
L187@P3: Regular tests:
L188@P3: • FBC, renal and liver profile prior to each cycle
L189@P3: • Blood glucose prior to each cycle
L190@P3: • TFTs prior to each cycle
L191@P3: • Cortisol as clinically indicated
L192@P3: Disease monitoring:
L193@P3: Disease monitoring should be in line with the patient’s treatment plan and any other test/s as directed by
L194@P3: the supervising Consultant.
L195@P3: DOSE MODIFICATIONS:
L196@P3: • Any treatment modification should be discussed with a Consultant
L197@P3: • Dose escalation or reduction is not recommended. Dosing delay or discontinuation may be required
L198@P3: based on individual safety and tolerability
L199@P3: • Management of immune-related adverse reactions may require withholding of a dose or
L200@P3: permanent discontinuation of nivolumab in combination with ipilimumab therapy and institution
L201@P3: of systemic high-dose corticosteroids (see Table 4)
L202@P3: • If immunosuppression with corticosteroids is used to treat an adverse reaction, a taper of at least
L203@P3: 1 month duration should be initiated upon improvement. Rapid tapering may lead to worsening or
L204@P3: recurrence of the adverse reaction. Non-corticosteroid immunosuppressive therapy should be
L205@P3: added if there is worsening or no improvement despite corticosteroid use. Nivolumab in
L206@P3: combination with ipilimumab should not be resumed while the patient is receiving
L207@P3: immunosuppressive doses of corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive therapy. Prophylactic
L208@P3: antibiotics should be used to prevent opportunistic infections in patients receiving
L209@P3: immunosuppressive therapy
L210@P3: • Nivolumab in combination with ipilimumab must be permanently discontinued for:
L211@P3: - Any severe immune-related adverse reaction that recurs
L212@P3: - Any life-threatening immune-related adverse reaction
L213@P3: - Any grade 4 or recurrent grade 3 adverse reactions, persistent grade 2 or 3 adverse
L214@P3: reactions despite management
L215@P3: • When nivolumab is administered in combination with ipilimumab, if either agent is withheld, the
L216@P3-4: other agent should also be withheld. If dosing is resumed after a delay, either the combination NCCP National SACT Regimen

L379@P6: Immune-related endocrinopathies
L380@P6: Patients should be monitored for clinical signs and symptoms of endocrinopathies and for hyperglycaemia and changes in thyroid function (at the
L381@P6: start of treatment, periodically during treatment, and as indicated based on clinical evaluation). Patients may present with fatigue, headache,
L382@P6: mental status changes, abdominal pain, unusual bowel habits, and hypotension, or nonspecific symptoms which may resemble other causes such as
L383@P6: brain metastasis or underlying disease. Unless an alternate aetiology has been identified, signs or symptoms of endocrinopathies should be
L384@P6: considered immune-related
L385@P6: Symptomatic Grade 2 or 3
L386@P6: hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism,
L387@P6: hypophysitis,
L388@P6: Grade 2 adrenal insufficiency
L389@P6: Grade 4 hypothyroidism
